preamble: Araucaria has 18 down of the 19, which is being treated with 13 15. This puzzle was originally published in the December issue of the magazine, 1 Across.

clue.text: Subject to town hall causing milieu's panic

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to put under the control of the local council

indicators.note: causing here means bringing about a new state of the letters, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's surroundings are thrown into a fluster, sending them to the council offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' signals that MILIEUSPANIC (the S of milieu's counts) is rearranged. 'Subject' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a service under the ownership or control of the local council is the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: 18 down worker gives coat to factory girl and father of archbishop's killer?

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill
Ann is a girl's name
Reginald FitzUrse was one of the knights who killed Archbishop Thomas Becket; Fitz means son of, so his father is Urse

explanation.surface: A question about a worker handing a coat to a mill girl and to the father of Becket's murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitz- in old surnames means 'son of', so FitzUrse's father is Urse. The UK charity Macmillan Cancer Support funds specialist nurses for people with cancer.
explanation.definitionFit: These specialist nurses from a UK charity care for people living with cancer, so they are cancer workers.

clue.text: Northern ocean hides love which could give ultimate 13 15

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something able to provide end-of-life palliative care

indicators.note: the northern ocean hides love, so one piece is tucked inside the other

parts.note: N for northern plus the Arctic, the northern ocean
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Northern seas hide affection, which might offer comfort at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong painkilling drugs such as morphine are used to ease suffering in the final stages of terminal illness.

clue.text: French writer passed, only first out of university

indicators.note: out of here means the chosen letter is removed from the word for a university

parts.note: a campus is a university's grounds, standing for the university itself

indicators.note: only first means just the opening letter of the word passed is taken

explanation.surface: A French author has died, and only the leader has left the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed' looks like 'died', but only its first letter P counts. That P comes 'out of' CAMPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist and philosopher, author of The Outsider, so he is a French writer.

clue.text: Overplay muddle over old Frenchman

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next one
muddle means the letters of the word overplay are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is caught up in a muddle from overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the anagram of OVERPLAY above O.
explanation.definitionFit: Parleyvoo is old British slang for a Frenchman, from 'parlez-vous', a phrase English speakers heard from French people.

clue.text: Hang about to see the Queen of Italy?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
IT is the international code for Italy
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A tourist idles about, hoping to catch sight of Italy's queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger or hang around somewhere with no clear purpose is the same idea as to hang about.

clue.text: Scamp item to expand 19, for example

parts.note: the word is split into S and camp, and a tent is a camp
the word is split into S and camp, and a tent is a camp

explanation.surface: A rascal is a device for widening a body passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Scamp' into S + camp, and camp gives TENT. 'Scamp' reads as a rascal but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mesh tube inserted to hold open a narrowed passage such as the gullet is this medical device.

clue.text: Accident on motorway summit?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI with the figure 1 as I
Shap is the summit of the M6 motorway in Cumbria, its highest point

explanation.surface: An accident happens on the motorway at its highest point.
explanation.walkthrough: Shap is a famous high pass on the M6 motorway in Cumbria, England, often hit by bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlucky incident or minor accident is a synonym in everyday use.

clue.text: Case lacking in posture

indicators.note: lacking means the following word is taken away from the first

parts.note: an instance is a case or example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suitcase with poor posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes IN out of INSTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The way someone holds their body when standing is their posture or bearing.

clue.text: Encounter dog's home

parts.note: in means at home
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Meeting someone at the dogs' home.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog's home is IN (at home) with CUR, with IN first.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet with or come up against something, usually unwelcome, such as debts or blame.

clue.text: Araucaria beginning to recite old poetry books, bringing Christmas cheer

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so the setter's name gives me

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of recite is used

parts.note: rime is an old spelling of rhyme, poetry
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: The setter starts reading old verse from books, spreading festive joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun, laughter and festive jollity is the cheer of the Christmas season.

clue.text: Man with a first having common sense? That's terrible

parts.note: he is a man
I is the Roman numeral one, a first
nous is British slang for common sense

explanation.surface: A man with a first-class degree and practical sense? That would be dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is British informal for common sense or shrewdness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shockingly evil or wicked, as a crime may be, is an extreme form of terrible.

clue.text: Scouse blues go green in time for energy supplier

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time, and E.ON is an energy supply company
vert is green in heraldry, from French

explanation.surface: Liverpool fans of the blue side going eco-friendly with their power company.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse means from Liverpool; this football club plays in blue, hence 'the Blues'. EON is both time and the power firm E.ON; 'go' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Liverpool football club wears blue and is nicknamed the Toffees and the Blues.

clue.text: Friendly (say) vicar at ease (say) with arrangement for coping with 18 down

indicators.note: the first (say) means friendly is to be spoken and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly

indicators.note: with arrangement means the letters that follow are put in a new order
the second (say) means ease is spoken, and it sounds like two letter Es

parts.note: spoken aloud, ease is the plural of the letter E

explanation.surface: A friendly vicar, relaxed, working out how to cope with illness.
explanation.walkthrough: PALLY said aloud gives PALLI; EASE said aloud is 'E's', so EE. 'with arrangement' shuffles VICARAT and EE together into ATIVECARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment aimed at relieving pain and symptoms rather than curing a disease is how serious illness is managed.

clue.text: Corrupt dealing with crime, the French abandoning the leader of the march?

indicators.note: abandoning means the French article is dropped from the longer phrase

parts.note: marching starts on the left foot, so the left boot leads
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A corrupt deal involving crime, with the French giving up the man at the head of the parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the leader of the march' is not a person: a march begins 'left, right', so THE LEFT BOOT leads. 'abandoning' removes LE.
explanation.definitionFit: This old legal term names the offence of taking back stolen goods or a bribe in return for not prosecuting the thief.

clue.text: See 13
Gray's works (in two volumes?) contain opening of Byzantine controversy

indicators.note: contain means the doubled piece holds the next letter inside it
in two volumes means the reworked letters appear twice over
works means the letters of the poet's name are worked into a new order

parts.note: Thomas Gray, the poet

indicators.note: opening of means just the first letter of Byzantine is taken

explanation.surface: A poet's collected works in two parts contain the start of a Byzantine dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' admits the joke: a poet's collected works printed as two volumes means the reworked name appears twice, with the Byzantine opening letter wedged between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Argy-bargy is British informal for a noisy quarrel or dispute, a lighter word for controversy.

clue.text: Plant reported to be enemy to skin complaint

indicators.note: reported to be means the words are spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a foe is an enemy, and tinea is the fungal skin complaint ringworm

explanation.surface: A plant said to be hostile to a skin problem.
explanation.walkthrough: FOE + TINEA said together gives the shrub's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen shrub, often grown in hedges for its red young leaves, is a garden plant.

clue.text: 101o under the ice?

parts.note: 101 is split into 100, C in Roman numerals, and the figure one
101 is split into 100, C in Roman numerals, and the figure one

explanation.surface: A temperature of 101 degrees under the ice, a fever in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'o' is a degree sign: 101° reads as a fever, but only 101 counts, as C (100) plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-cream wafer cone sits beneath the scoop of ice cream it holds.

clue.text: Sign of growth

definitions.meaning: a malignant tumour is a growth

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the fourth sign of the zodiac and a malignant tumour, a harmful growth in the body.

clue.text: Food transporter heard to gradually reduce an endless effusion

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is spoken aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: to ease off is to reduce gradually

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the outpouring is dropped

parts.note: a gush is an effusion, an outpouring

explanation.surface: A food carrier is said to slow down after a great outpouring.
explanation.walkthrough: EASE OFF said aloud gives OESOPH; 'endless' cuts the last letter from A GUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullet, the muscular tube carrying swallowed food from the throat to the stomach.

clue.text: Fat round Poles at end of day

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
N and S are the North and South Poles

explanation.surface: Fat spread around Poles at the close of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The time when the sun goes down marks the close of the day.

clue.text: Beast of Oz whose subject was cats

definitions.meaning: T. S. Eliot, nicknamed Old ..., wrote Old ... Book of Practical Cats

explanation.definitionFit: It is an Australian marsupial and also the nickname of T. S. Eliot, author of the poems behind the musical Cats.

clue.text: Place(s) of non-vintage vintage?

parts.note: a non-vintage wine is new, not aged
vintage port is a fortified wine from a declared year

explanation.surface: A question about where new wine and fine old wine are found.
explanation.walkthrough: '(s)' admits there are several towns with this name, in Wales, on the Isle of Wight and in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Several towns share this name, in Wales, on the Isle of Wight and in Rhode Island, so it names more than one place.

clue.text: Dimension accompanying outside number

indicators.note: outside means the first word is placed around the second

parts.note: with means accompanying
D is the Roman numeral 500, a number

explanation.surface: A dimension going along with an external number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts WITH around D.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth from side to side is one of the measurements of an object, a dimension.

clue.text: Food related to cake of soap?

definitions.text: Food related to cake of soap?

parts.words: Food related to cake of soap?
parts.note: a sweet sticky currant bun named after a spa town shares its name with where a cake of soap is used

explanation.walkthrough: A cake of soap belongs in the tub; this sweet bun, named after the Somerset spa town, shares that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar-topped currant roll from the English spa city counts as food that has a link with washing.

clue.text: Cook said to be lawman and impresario

indicators.note: said to be means the word is spoken aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: to boil is to cook

explanation.surface: A chef is said to be both a policeman and a showbusiness promoter.
explanation.walkthrough: The lawman is Robert Boyle of Boyle's law on gases; the impresario is presumably film and stage director Danny Boyle, who staged the 2012 Olympics opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to Robert, the physicist behind the gas law, and to Danny, who directed the London Olympics ceremony.

clue.text: Complete very large reproduction with look at 19 etc

parts.note: to end is to complete
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a copy is a reproduction

explanation.surface: Finishing an outsize reproduction with a look at the gullet.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing label for very large sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical examination uses a camera on a flexible tube to look inside the body, such as the gullet.

clue.text: See 1 down
Bargain keeping mum to deal with 18 down

indicators.note: keeping means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: a cheapy, or cheapie, is a bargain
mum is a mother

explanation.surface: A bargain that keeps Mum's illness at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers lists the -y spelling beside the more usual -ie for this informal word for a bargain; the surface's mum keeping quiet is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug treatment used against tumours is a standard way to treat cancer.
